name: DATE_DIFF
description: Returns the difference between two dates in the specified unit, as date2 - date1: the first argument is the START and the second is the END.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Unit for result (YEAR, MONTH, WEEK, DAY, HOUR, MINUTE, SECOND)

examples.title: Calculate age
examples.sql: SELECT DATE_DIFF(birthdate, CURRENT_DATE, YEAR) as age FROM users

examples.title: Days since event
examples.sql: SELECT DATE_DIFF(event_date, CURRENT_DATE, DAY) as days_ago FROM events

examples.title: Hours between timestamps
examples.sql: SELECT DATE_DIFF(start_time, end_time, HOUR) as duration_hours FROM sessions

notes: Returns a negative value if date2 is before date1
DATEDIFF is NOT an alias of this function. It is MySQL's, and subtracts the other way round (expr1 - expr2). See HELP DATEDIFF.
TIMESTAMPDIFF is the ODBC/JDBC spelling and takes the unit first; MySQL defines it as dt2 - dt1, which is what this function already computes.
